subject: Biotechnology
title: Bioreactor Design
description: A quick, practical guide to Bioreactor Design.

hook.text: A bioreactor is a living factory — its design determines whether cells thrive or die at industrial scale.

buildup.text: Stirred-tank reactors use impellers to mix nutrients and oxygen — the workhorse of pharma manufacturing.

discovery.text: Airlift reactors use gas bubbles for gentle mixing — perfect for fragile mammalian cells that shear forces destroy.

twist.text: Scaling from 1-liter lab flasks to 20,000-liter production tanks is not linear — mixing, heat, and oxygen all change.

climax.text: Single-use bioreactors use disposable plastic bags — eliminating cleaning validation and reducing contamination risk.

punchline.text: Shape the vessel, shape the product — bioreactor design is biotech's foundation.

quiz.question: Why is scaling bioreactors from lab to production scale challenging?
options: Larger bioreactors use different types of microorganisms
Mixing, heat transfer, and oxygen delivery behave differently at larger volumes, requiring redesign
Production-scale bioreactors cannot maintain sterile conditions
